# Save compatibility for generated rings

## Goal

Guarantee that switching the content source to a generator cannot damage an
existing war save: a stored ring is preserved byte-for-byte and a fresh ring
generates.

**User story:** As a player, loading my existing war keeps exactly the map I
have been playing, and starting a war (or opening a ring) gives me a generated
map that survives reload unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **Existing saves remain playable and unchanged**: a stored ring (full or partial) is never regenerated or discarded; a fresh/empty ring generates from the seed; defensive parse and migration behaviour is covered by tests.
- A payload written before this change (authored ring hexes, ids `hex-r1-*` / `hex-r2-*`, a stored `frontierTick`, absent `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels`) loads and round-trips unchanged: every hex id, coordinate, held state, aggression and defender is byte-for-byte identical after a save/load cycle, with no schema version bump.
- A partial ring (some hexes stored, fewer than the full ring) is preserved exactly and is never padded up to the generated ring's size; the next ring opened is generated from the seed.
- A fresh or empty ring generates from `payload.seed` and round-trips: save → load → the same generated hexes (no re-roll on reload), because generation is a pure function of the persisted seed and ring index.
- Defensive parse behaviour is asserted: a corrupt or absent `seed`, a non-object ring, a malformed hex row and an unknown extra field all degrade to a playable payload (or a clean null) rather than throwing, matching `parseHangarWarPayload`'s existing contract.
- Migration coverage is explicit in tests for: legacy authored payload, fresh payload, partial ring, corrupt ring, and large ring index (e.g. ring 7) round-trip.
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Notes & assumptions

- No schema change is intended (producer Q2 = A): the seed and `ring.ringIndex`
  are the only generation inputs and both are already persisted. If an
  implementation detail makes a new field unavoidable, it must be additive,
  optional and migrated by field presence — and that deviation must be recorded
  in the item's completion comment.
- The stored-ring invariant is the safety property: generation may only fill an
  **empty** ring, never rewrite a non-empty one.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.ts` — `parseHangarWarPayload`, `createDefaultPayload`, `loadHangarWarPayload` / `saveHangarWarPayload` (field-presence migration, no version bump).
- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.ts` — the storage seam the round-trip tests drive.
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts` — `HangarWarPayload` / `HexState` field presence rules.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarWarStore.test.ts` — parse/migration tests to extend.
- `src/core/hangarWar/storage.test.ts` — save/load round-trip tests to extend.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` — `materialiseRing`'s stored-ring invariant (the behaviour under test).

## Related work

- Parent **AH-0MWL4SNKR001CDAA** — Procedurally generated Hex Map (epic); Q2 = A
  producer decision (pure function of `(payload.seed, ringIndex)`, generated on
  demand; only `HexState` persisted).
- **AH-0MWH42DWQ004SAOJ** — the defender upgrade snapshot: the precedented
  additive/optional field-presence migration pattern to follow.
- **AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU** — the `weaponLevels` / `powerUpLevels` optional fields
  an old payload legitimately lacks.

# Gym and game parity for generated rings

## Goal

Prove the gym and the game render and resolve exactly the same generated ring,
so the headless harness is trustworthy evidence for a seed-derived map.

**User story:** As a test/agent, `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as
the game, so what I measure in the gym is what the player plays.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Unit, property and integration tests cover determinism, distinct-seed variety, invariant enforcement across many seeds and large ring indices, the grant-economy rule, and the save/load round-trip; `GymHexWar` renders the same generated model as the game.
- `GymHexWar` obtains its ring definitions from the same seed-aware source as the game (no gym-only authored fixture), and an explicit parity test asserts the gym and game read models are deep-equal for at least three seeds and ring indices 1, 2 and 3.
- `GymMiniBoss`'s HEX control resolves its deployment definition (the ring's weapon hex) from the generator for the payload's seed and ring index, so the boss body colour and opening volley come from the generated weapon hex rather than `hex-r1-6` fixture data.
- A parity assertion covers the intel read model (boss, strengths/weaknesses, aggression, grant) and the weapon-hex/special-mission flags, so a gym-only divergence fails loudly.
- `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`'s hex-ring rows are updated to describe the generated source and the new parity test as the evidence column (the docs sweep item may polish wording; this item's row must be accurate).
- Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

- Parity means the same **pure read model**, not pixel equality: both sides call

# Defusal rule in the pure frontier tick

The engine slice of the pre-emptive counter-push (AH-0MWL7P5T50030229): a
**winning** deployment at the origin of a queued attack cancels that attack
inside the pure tick, and is recorded so the report can announce it.

## Target outcome

Striking first is mechanically real. Win at the hex that is about to hit you and
the queued attack never lands; lose and it resolves exactly as it does today.

## Scope

- `FrontierTickOptions` gains `deploymentWon?: boolean` (default `false` =
  today's behaviour), documented as a **transient** input derived from the
  deployment — never persisted (parent Q4 assumption, AC6 holds).
- In the pending-attack loop, each queued attack's **natural** pre-redistribution
  origin is derived from the **input** `payload` (not the redistributed `next`)
  and with **no** origin exclusion, so the check asks "would this attack have
  originated at the hex I am attacking?" (parent Q3 = A).
- When `deploymentWon === true` and that origin equals `playerAttackingHexId`,
  the attack is cancelled: skip `resolveAttack`/`applyDefence` for it and record a
  defusal entry (attacked hex id, origin id, force) on `FrontierTickRecord`.
- Defusal wins over the sibling fair-origin fallback (parent Q2 = A): a defused
  attack is cancelled outright and never re-originates from another unheld
  neighbour, so the announcement is literally true.
- A loss (or any other case) resolves exactly as today, fair-origin rule intact.
- The defusal check is pure arithmetic and consumes **no** seeded draw.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `FrontierTickOptions.deploymentWon?: boolean` exists, defaults to `false`, and is documented in `hexDefence.ts` as transient (no payload field, no schema version bump).
- On a win whose deployment hex is a queued attack's natural pre-redistribution origin, that attack produces no `HexDefenceRecord`, the target's defence is not resolved on that tick, and `pendingAttacks` is consumed as today.
- The cancelled attack is recorded on `FrontierTickRecord` (attacked hex, origin id, force) so no surface re-derives it; the field is additive and absent/empty for an ordinary tick.
- On a loss at the same origin the tick resolves exactly as today, including re-origination from the next most aggressive unheld neighbour.
- With `deploymentWon` omitted or `false` the tick's payload, clock and record are deep-equal to the pre-change behaviour, and the 70 % attack-chance draw order and value are unchanged.
- A defusal consumes no seeded draw: replaying `(payload, seed, tick, attackingHex, deploymentWon)` yields deep-equal results, and the draw after a defusal equals the draw without it.
- Every existing `resolveDefence` and `runFrontierTick` test passes unchanged.

- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: A winning deployment whose target hex is the origin of a queued attack cancels that attack in the same payload write: the target hex defence is not resolved on that tick, and the rolled-in defence report announces the defusal.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: A losing deployment at that origin leaves the queued attack intact and it resolves exactly as today, including the sibling fair-origin rule.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: An ordinary deployment with no queued attack at its origin is byte-identical to today's tick: the existing resolveDefence, attackingNeighbour and runFrontierTick suites pass unchanged and the 70% attack-chance draw order is unchanged.
- Covers the parent acceptance criterion: No new persisted field: the queued attack origin is derived by attackingNeighbour on the stored payload before this tick redistribution, so a save written before this change loads and resolves exactly as today.

## Minimal Implementation

- Add the option beside the shipped `playerAttackingHexId` and normalise it to a boolean with a `false` default.
- Derive the natural origin once per queued attack from the input payload via the shipped `attackingNeighbour` with no exclusion list, then branch before `resolveAttack`.
- Accumulate defusal entries in a local array and attach them to the record.
- Extend the existing pending-attack loop; do not restructure the redistribution or the 70 % draw path.

**Key Files:**

- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/hexDefence.test.ts`
- `src/core/hangarWar/types.ts`

## Dependencies

- Blocked by the pure-core red-first test gate (sibling item created before this one).

## Deliverables

The defusal rule in the pure, replayable tick with its record, pinned by tests.

## Notes

- `types.ts` needs **no** schema change; confirm only (AC6).
- Accepted caveat from intake Q3: the pre-redistribution origin can differ from
  the origin the resolver would have used after redistribution, so a defusal may
  name an origin today's resolver would not have attacked from. Accepted by the
  producer; record it in the code comment beside the rule.

- A seeded replay sweep over mixed defusing/non-defusing ticks yields deep-equal results across reruns, and a defusal leaves subsequent ticks' draws unchanged.

Part of `Close the one-level mineral income gap that collection cannot recover (AH-0MWSGD3QF004RWAQ)` — the shared-core slice that gives the headless arena a seam into the game's real mineral payout without importing Phaser.

# Goal

As the project, I want the game's mineral kill-payout **decision** (re-drop count, deposit threshold, Salvage fold) to live in one Phaser-free module consumed by both the scene seam and the headless arena, so the arena can model the real rule and the two can never drift.

# Problem

`resolveMineralKillPayout` / `resolveMineralKillDrops` in `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` construct Phaser `Mineral` display objects, so the headless arena (`src/ai/eval/arena.ts`, Node/vitest, no Phaser) cannot consume the rule. Today the arena therefore invents its own supply (a static 18-point field).

# Target outcome

- A pure, Phaser-free module (e.g. `src/core/mineralPayout.ts`) owning the payout **decision**: the doubled re-drop count (`MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER × round(collected + bonus)`), the deposit decision (`redropCount + salvageBonus ≥ MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD` ⇒ one deposit worth `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`), and the small-asteroid yield — all expressed as numbers, not game objects.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` consumes that decision and keeps its existing behaviour exactly (same draw order, same scatter, same deposit, same Salvage suppression) — the shared rule stays the single source of truth for the game and the gyms.
- The arena can import the decision module with no Phaser dependency.

# Definition of done

- The pure module has its own unit tests covering: the non-asteroid doubled count, a zero-collected bonus roll, the deposit threshold (including a surplus wreck paying one deposit), small vs large/medium asteroid, and the Salvage fold.
- `mineralKillDrops.ts` delegates to the pure module; its existing tests pass unchanged (behaviour-preserving refactor, no re-pinning).
- No new RNG draws are introduced: the bonus roll is exactly one draw per non-asteroid wreck, as today.
- Documentation (module doc comments, and `docs/BALANCING.md` where the rule is described) names the pure decision module as the single source.

# Constraints

- **Behaviour-preserving.** This slice must not change any game, gym or arena outcome; if a test pin moves, the refactor was not behaviour-preserving — fix the refactor, not the pin.
- No Phaser import in the pure module (guard it with a test that imports it in the headless environment).
- Determinism preserved: no wall-clock reads and no un-injected randomness in the pure decision (rng injected).

# Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` — the scene seam that will delegate to the pure module.
- `src/core/mineralPayout.ts` — the new Phaser-free decision module.
- `src/core/constants.ts` — `MINERAL_DROP_MULTIPLIER`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_THRESHOLD`, `MINERAL_DEPOSIT_VALUE`.
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` — `mineralRedropCount` / `collectMineral` (the rule's entity side).
- `src/entities/Mineral.ts` — the display object that stays Phaser-side.
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — the documented kill-drop rule.

# Acceptance Criteria

- A Phaser-free module owns the mineral kill-payout decision (count, deposit threshold, small-asteroid yield, Salvage fold) and is importable by the headless arena.
- `src/scenes/core/mineralKillDrops.ts` delegates to it with **no** behaviour change: its existing tests pass unmodified and no game/gym/arena figure moves.
- Unit tests cover the doubled count, the bonus roll, the deposit threshold and its surplus rule, the asteroid tiers and the Salvage fold.
- The pure module has no Phaser import and no un-injected randomness or wall-clock read (asserted by a test).
- The single-source-of-truth relationship is documented in the module doc comment and in `docs/BALANCING.md`.
- Impact section recorded.

# Dependencies

Blocked by `Test: record the arena-vs-game mineral divergence` — the divergence evidence this refactor serves.

# Impact

The arena can measure the game's real mineral payout instead of a harness constant, without duplicating the rule.

# Shared per-bullet time-scale seam

## Goal

*As an agent / gym user, I want the enemy-bullet advance to accept a per-bullet
time scale, so Chrono can slow only the bullets inside its field through one
shared implementation that the game and every gym run identically.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, constraint "**Shared-core discipline** — the
  per-bullet slowed dt belongs in `src/scenes/core/` (an optional per-bullet
  time-scale hook on `advanceWrappingBullets`) and every consumer passes the same
  resolver" and "**Backwards-compatible helper** — the per-bullet scale must be
  optional with today's uniform-dt behaviour as the default".
- Today's call sites: `PlayScene._advanceBullets` (~:5215),
  `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` (~:2183), `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690, currently raw `dt`).
- Adjacent, not in scope: **AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB — World slow-motion time scale**
  (blocked) must be able to compose its `teleportTimeScale()` multiplicatively
  with this seam; a pure, side-effect-free resolver keeps that possible. Do not
  implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `advanceWrappingBullets` accepts an **optional** per-bullet time-scale resolver (e.g. a trailing `resolveScale?: (bullet: T) => number` parameter); omitting it reproduces today's uniform-`dt` behaviour exactly, so every existing caller and test passes unchanged.
- With a resolver supplied, each bullet integrates position, ages `elapsed`, fades and expires on **its own** scaled dt inside a single call — two bullets in one call advance by different distances — so no scene can apply a scale twice.
- The resolver is consulted exactly once per bullet per call, using the bullet's pre-integration position, and the loop introduces no closure, array or object allocation per bullet (satisfied against the `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` budget test).
- Player bullets are untouched: `advancePlayerBullets` keeps its signature and behaviour, and a test asserts a Chrono-style resolver never reaches player bullets.
- The helper remains a **single** definition in `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard is extended if a new exported resolver helper appears, and it passes.
- The helper's doc comment states this is the one seam every scene uses for enemy-bullet time scaling (and the composition point for future world slow-motion).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the optional resolver parameter to `advanceWrappingBullets` and use `dt * scale` for ageing, integration, fade and expiry (one scale read per bullet, no allocation).
- Tests first: default path unchanged, per-bullet divergence, once-per-call invocation, ageing/fade coupling, player-bullet exclusion.

- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body / shared-symbol guard.

# Per-war starter draw, ownership and free auto-equip

## Summary

Give every fresh Hangar War a seeded, ring-1 starter weapon that it owns for the
war and auto-equips for the first deployment, replacing the catalogue's fixed
`starter: true` weapon ownership with the per-war record.

## Acceptance Criteria

_The parent acceptance criteria this item owns, restated verbatim so the plan's AC coverage is traceable:_

- A **fresh war** (`createDefaultPayload(<seed>)` or a first load with no save) draws one starter from **every purchasable ring-1 weapon** in the hangar catalogue (`kind === 'weapon'`, `minRing <= 1`, `isPurchasableEntry`) and **auto-equips** it in `activeLoadout.startingWeapons`, so the very first deployment (`buildHangarDeployment`) carries it as a starting weapon. The draw is **deterministic for the payload seed** (the same seed always yields the same starter; different seeds can yield different starters, and a seeded sweep shows every eligible entry is reachable). The drawn starter costs nothing — no minerals or cores are deducted, even when its catalogue price is non-zero. (this item implements and tests it.)
- **Existing saves are unchanged**: a stored payload keeps its current owned starter, loadout and hangar state (no re-roll on load, no loadout rewrite, no back-fill). Migration stays field-presence based, no schema version bump is required, and a legacy save's implicit starter remains `spread`; a legacy save's empty loadout is still filled by the existing hangar auto-fit on open, not by this change. (this item's migration/round-trip tests cover it.)
- A new pure module exports `starterWeaponPool(catalogue)` and
  `drawStarterWeaponId(seed, catalogue)`: the pool is every `kind === 'weapon'`
  entry with `minRing <= 1` and `isPurchasableEntry(entry)` (so `spread` is in
  the pool and grant-only entries are not), and the draw goes through
  `createHangarWarRng(seed).pick(...)` — no `Math.random()` anywhere in the path.
- `HangarState` gains the additive optional `starterWeaponId?: string`;
  `parseHangar` migrates it by field presence (absent stays absent, a present
  value is trimmed to a usable id) and `resolveStarterWeaponId(hangar,catalogue?)`
  returns it, falling back to `spread` when absent. No schema version bump.
- `createDefaultPayload(seed)` records the drawn id in `hangar.starterWeaponId`,
  owns it in `hangar.unlockedWeapons` and auto-equips it in
  `hangar.activeLoadout.startingWeapons`; banked minerals/cores stay `0`
  (the drawn starter is free even when its catalogue price is non-zero).
- `ownsEntry` reports the war's starter as owned even when a corrupt save
  dropped it from `unlockedWeapons`, so the fleet can never lose its free
  weapon; the catalogue's `starter: true` no longer marks any weapon (only
  `hull-1` stays a starter entry) and `STARTER_WEAPON_ID` is re-documented as
  the legacy fallback constant it now is.
- A **first load with no stored save** (`loadHangarWarPayload` against an empty
  store) yields that same fresh payload, so the very first war's starter is the
  seed's draw (no unseeded randomness on the load path).
- `buildHangarDeployment(payload)` for a fresh payload carries the drawn starter
  in the launch data's starting weapons (its permanent-level resolution is
  unchanged).
- Unit coverage: the tests from the test-first child go green, plus ownership
  and migration cases for a legacy hangar (no field) and a corrupt-starter case;
  `docs`/module docblocks touched here state the new rule (doc text itself is
  the documentation child's scope).

- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`

## Context (verified during AH-0MWWI3ONJ004QRR9)
The unlock-tree scrolling fix (AH-0MWWI3ONJ004QRR9) scrolled only the left `UNLOCKS` column, per that item's ACs. The right column derived by `hangarRightColumnLayout` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`) grows with the number of owned weapons: `buildHangarWeaponOptions` lists **every** id in `payload.hangar.unlockedWeapons`, with no page/window cap.

Worked example with 4 owned hulls + 9 owned weapons (+ the 2 modifiers):
- `weaponRowY` ends at y ≈ 372
- `modifierHeadingY` ≈ 398, modifier rows at ≈ 424 / 440
- `savedBuildHeadingY` ≈ 466, saved-build row ≈ 492

**Gym parity.** `GymHangar` renders the same `renderHangarScreen`; it gained an optional read-only `catalogue` launch field so a parity/capture fixture can exercise the grown tree without owning every weapon. It exposes `getUnlockScroll`/`scrollUnlockRows` seams. No gameplay/economy/catalogue behaviour changed (AC10).
